business_problem: EnBW needed a highly available and flexible data platform for Germany's growing fast-charging network and the apps and operations behind it.
solution_summary: EnBW standardized both sides of its e-mobility business on MongoDB Atlas so the charge point operator and electromobility provider teams could scale a rapidly expanding EV charging network with the same modern data platform. Atlas stores the infrastructure, customer-access, pricing, and operational data behind the mobility+ app and fast-charging grid, while scrum teams across CPO, EMP, iOS, and Android share a common platform through EnBW's internal OnePlatform resource. The move improved availability, performance, and flexibility versus earlier systems and gave operators direct visibility into cluster behavior and simple scaling controls. That foundation supports award-winning charging services and faster rollout of new mobility features as the network grows.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores charging infrastructure and customer-access data for EnBW's mobility services.

data_flow: Charging-infrastructure and customer-access data from EnBW's CPO and EMP systems is stored in MongoDB Atlas, then surfaced to iOS and Android apps and operations teams that monitor availability, pricing, and scale across the network.
business_outcome: EnBW improved availability and visibility across its charging infrastructure, scales more easily, and keeps shipping customer-facing mobility features faster.
metrics: EnBW employs some 26,000 people and supplies around 5.5 million customers.
EnBW aims to have 2,500 fast-charging stations available across Germany by 2025, with an annual investment of €100 million.
The EnBW HyperNet offers EV-drivers more than 300,000 charging points in 16 European countries.
architecture_clues: Both the CPO and EMP units now run on Atlas in parallel.
Atlas is made available internally as a group solution through OnePlatform.
The Atlas interface gives operators full visibility and quick cluster-size changes.
evidence_quotes: The CPO side of the operation had adopted MongoDB from the outset in 2019.
The CPO side of the business used Atlas from the outset, so now the two units are both running on Atlas in parallel.
